project.name: RONL Business API
project.description: A secure, multi-tenant platform enabling Dutch municipalities to offer government digital services. Implements the Business API Layer pattern between IAM (Keycloak) and BPMN process execution (Operaton), with AI chat via MCP providers.

nodes.name: TaskFormViewer
nodes.summary: Exported component that imperatively mounts a bpmn-io form-js form inside a React ref container, handles submit/complete lifecycle, and shows a fallback button when no form schema exists.

nodes.name: GegevenswoordenboekV2
nodes.summary: Exported V2 component with search form, language switcher, and Skosmos iframe that deep-links into vocabulary search results.

nodes.name: NoAccessPanel.tsx

nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately re-uses all V1 CaseworkerDashboard section components as a compatibility shim so the V2 shell is functional from day one before each section is redesigned.

nodes.name: SectionRouter
nodes.summary: Exported dispatcher component that evaluates role/org-type gates from MODES config and routes section IDs to their corresponding React components.

nodes.name: findGateFor
nodes.summary: Walks the MODES configuration tree to find requiredRoles and requiredOrgTypes for a given section ID, returning null for ungated sections.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses useMemo with a ctx object (now + userSub) to efficiently derive filter counts and visible task lists in a single pass over the task array.

nodes.name: TakenInbox
nodes.summary: Exported V2 task inbox with filter rail, deadline-sorted list, detail pane with process data table, claim action, and embedded form viewer.

nodes.name: DecisionViewer
nodes.summary: Exported component that fetches process variables and decision document template, rendering the letter layout or falling back to a read-only form-js view.

nodes.name: renderTipTapNode
nodes.summary: Recursively renders a TipTap/ProseMirror AST node to React elements with mark application (bold, italic, underline) and variable interpolation.

nodes.name: useProfielData
nodes.summary: Exported hook that wraps businessApi.hr.profile with loading/error state and a memoized load function for on-demand fetching.

nodes.name: CaseworkerDashboard.tsx
nodes.summary: V1 caseworker portal page with top navigation, tenant-aware left panel, and a content area that renders one of many dashboard sections based on active selection. Handles Keycloak authentication, multi-tenant theming, and task/IOU counters in the nav badges.
nodes.languageNotes: Section memory pattern: stores last-selected section per top-nav page so navigating away and back restores the user's previous position.

nodes.name: CaseworkerDashboard
nodes.summary: Root page component orchestrating Keycloak auth init, tenant theme/config loading, section routing via a large switch, and the full chrome (top nav bar, left panel, content area).

nodes.name: api.ts
nodes.summary: Central API client module for the frontend, providing an authenticated axios instance with Keycloak token injection and a structured businessApi object covering health, decisions, processes, tasks, portal content, HR, RIP, admin, capacity claims, edocs, and MCP chat streams.
nodes.languageNotes: MCP chatStream is implemented as an async generator over SSE (Server-Sent Events) using the Fetch API directly (not axios) to support streaming responses; all other calls use axios.

nodes.name: tenant.ts
nodes.summary: Multi-tenant configuration service that loads tenant registry from a static tenants.json, resolves per-tenant theme and feature flags, and applies CSS custom properties for branding.

nodes.name: loadTenantConfigs
nodes.summary: Fetches and caches the tenant registry from /tenants.json, populating module-level singletons for tenant lookup.

nodes.name: initializeTenantTheme
nodes.summary: Ensures tenant configs are loaded, resolves the config for a municipality, and applies its CSS theme variables if the tenant is enabled.

nodes.name: applyTenantTheme
nodes.summary: Applies a TenantTheme object to the document root as CSS custom properties for primary, secondary, and accent colors.

nodes.name: formatDate.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal utility exporting a single formatDate function that converts an ISO date string to a Dutch locale long-form date string.

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.summary: Converts an ISO date string to a Dutch locale full date string (day month year) using Intl.DateTimeFormat via toLocaleDateString.

nodes.name: ProtectedRoute
nodes.summary: Higher-order React component that guards a route by checking whether the authenticated Keycloak user holds the required role, redirecting to the login page if not.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Top-level React component that sets up the BrowserRouter with public and role-protected routes for the caseworker application.

nodes.name: McpChatSection
nodes.summary: Large React component providing an MCP-backed AI chat interface with model and source selection, streaming message display, and send/clear controls.

nodes.name: CaseworkerDashboardV2

nodes.name: LoginChoice
nodes.summary: React page component rendering IDP selection buttons (DigiD, eHerkenning, etc.) and a changelog trigger, storing the selected IDP in sessionStorage before redirecting.

nodes.name: modes.config.ts
nodes.summary: Configuration module that defines the complete MODES array (navigation rail structure for the V2 dashboard) and exports utility functions for visibility gating, section lookups, and searchable index generation.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports MODES constant plus four named utility functions used throughout the V2 dashboard for role/tenant gating and command-palette indexing.

nodes.name: isRailItemVisible
nodes.summary: Determines whether a navigation rail item should be shown based on tenant section IDs, required roles, and organisation type constraints.

nodes.name: tenantSectionIdsFrom
nodes.summary: Derives the set of section IDs enabled for a tenant from its left-panel configuration object.

nodes.name: findModeForSection
nodes.summary: Searches the MODES array to find which mode key owns a given section ID.

nodes.name: allSearchableSections
nodes.summary: Returns a flat list of all non-header rail items across all modes, used as the source for command-palette search indexing.

nodes.name: changelog-data.ts
nodes.summary: Static data module exporting the full application changelog as a structured object with versioned entries, sections, and individual change items.

nodes.name: keycloak.ts
nodes.summary: Keycloak service module that instantiates the singleton Keycloak client and exposes helper functions for extracting the authenticated user profile and bearer token.

nodes.name: getUser
nodes.summary: Reads the Keycloak tokenParsed payload to construct and return a KeycloakUser object containing name, email, municipality, and roles.

nodes.name: getToken
nodes.summary: Returns the current Keycloak bearer token string for use in API request headers.

nodes.name: jwt.middleware.ts
nodes.summary: Provides JWT authentication middleware for the Express backend, including JWKS-based token validation, user extraction, role-based access control, and assurance-level enforcement. Exports four middleware/factory functions consumed by nearly every route in the application.

nodes.name: jwtMiddleware
nodes.summary: Core Express middleware that validates Bearer JWTs from the Authorization header, attaches the extracted user to req.user, and measures authentication latency.

nodes.name: requireRoles
nodes.summary: Middleware factory that returns an Express handler enforcing that the authenticated user holds at least one of the specified roles, returning 403 otherwise.

nodes.name: requireAssuranceLevel
nodes.summary: Middleware factory that enforces a minimum DigiD/eHerkenning assurance level on the authenticated user, rejecting requests that do not meet the configured threshold.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Main entry point for the backend Express server that wires all middleware, mounts every route module, initializes the database, registers LLM and MCP providers, and starts the HTTP listener. Acts as the application composition root.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports 27 project-internal modules, composing the entire backend application from discrete service and route modules.

nodes.name: startServer
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the application: initialises the database, starts the external task worker, registers all LLM and MCP providers, connects MCP clients, and begins listening on the configured port.

nodes.name: audit.middleware.ts
nodes.summary: Implements request-level audit logging middleware that intercepts response writes, captures HTTP status and body, derives an audit action from the request path, and persists structured audit log entries to an in-memory queue and backing store.

nodes.name: auditMiddleware
nodes.summary: Express middleware that monkey-patches res.json and res.end to intercept response data, derives an audit action from the request path, and records an audit log entry after each request completes.

nodes.name: auditLog
nodes.summary: Utility function for recording explicit audit events from route handlers, wrapping createAuditLog with request context extraction.

nodes.name: createAuditLog
nodes.summary: Creates and enqueues an audit log entry, logs it via the structured logger, and asynchronously persists it to the audit service.

nodes.name: brp.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Express routes for the BRP (Basisregistratie Personen) citizen data integration, proxying authenticated requests to the Dutch municipal persons register.

nodes.name: capacity.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Express routes for capacity management, delegating to the Operaton BPMN service for process-driven capacity queries and updates.

nodes.name: edocs.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Express routes for the eDocs document management integration, providing authenticated access to document retrieval and management operations.

nodes.name: hr.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Express routes for HR (human resources) data, bridging authenticated HTTP requests to the Operaton process engine for HR-related queries.

nodes.name: m2m.routes.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Largest route file at 553 lines; implements an operation allowlist pattern and a type-inference helper for converting JSON payloads into Operaton variable format.

nodes.name: toOperatonVariables
nodes.summary: Converts a plain key-value input object into the Operaton variable format by inferring each value's type using inferType.

nodes.name: mcp.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Express routes for the MCP (Model Context Protocol) AI chat interface, streaming LLM responses to clients via Server-Sent Events and delegating tool calls through the McpRegistry.

nodes.name: rip.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Defines Express routes for the RIP (Regelingen en Informatievoorziening Personen) integration, proxying authenticated requests to the Operaton-backed service for personal regulation lookups.

nodes.name: auth.types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines shared TypeScript interfaces and enums for authentication and authorisation, including AuthenticatedUser, AssuranceLevel (DigiD/eHerkenning levels), MandateInfo, and OrganisationType.

nodes.name: config.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Uses a custom parseEnvArray/Int/Bool helper pattern rather than a schema validation library; validateConfig collects all errors before throwing, enabling comprehensive startup diagnostics.

nodes.name: validateConfig
nodes.summary: Validates the parsed configuration object, collecting all missing or invalid required fields and throwing a descriptive error at startup if any are found.

nodes.name: logger.ts
nodes.summary: Provides a structured logging factory built on the configured log transport, exposing createLogger(module) for per-module named loggers with debug/info/warn/error levels.

nodes.name: createLogger
nodes.summary: Factory function that creates a module-scoped logger wrapping the configured log transport, providing debug, info, warn, and error methods.

nodes.name: DvtpStartSection
nodes.summary: Default-exported React component that renders a start button for the DVTP process, managing started/error state and calling onNavigateToTasks callback on successful submission.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses OpenAPI 3.1 discriminator pattern (BewoningMetPeildatum / BewoningMetPeriode) for polymorphic query types, and RFC7807 problem+json for error responses. Schemas support partially-unknown dates via the AbstractDatum hierarchy.

nodes.languageNotes: The largest of the three specs at 1953 lines. Uses discriminator-based polymorphism for both the request (PersonenQuery with 7 subtypes) and response (PersonenQueryResponse with 7 matching subtypes). Supports field filtering via a 'fields' array parameter of up to 130 field paths.

nodes.name: POST /personen
nodes.summary: Searches and retrieves persons from the Dutch Base Registration of Persons (BRP) using one of seven query strategies, with optional field filtering and support for deceased persons.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses OpenAPI 3.0.3 (not 3.1 like the other two specs). Models four types of residence via the AbstractVerblijfplaatsVoorkomen discriminator hierarchy: domestic address (Adres), foreign address (VerblijfplaatsBuitenland), location (Locatie), and unknown (VerblijfplaatsOnbekend). Includes RNI (non-resident) registration support.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces RONL Business API: a secure, multi-tenant platform that lets Dutch municipalities offer government digital services to residents. It places the project in its architectural context — the Business API Layer that sits between a municipality's Keycloak IAM system and the Operaton BPMN engine — and lists the full technology stack. Reading this first frames every code file that follows.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: The Express server entry point is where the entire backend is wired together. It registers JWT authentication, audit, and tenant middleware in sequence, then mounts all route modules (process, task, BRP, eDocs, MCP, and more) before starting to listen. Tracing the import list here is the fastest way to build a mental map of every subsystem the backend exposes.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript modules use top-level `import` statements resolved at build time. The order of `app.use()` calls in Express is significant: middleware registered first runs first, so JWT validation is always applied before business-logic routes.

tour.title: Shared Type Contracts
tour.description: The @ronl/shared package is the single source of truth for TypeScript types that cross the frontend-backend boundary: API response envelopes, authentication and assurance-level enums, Operaton BPMN variable shapes, and tenant configuration structures. Because every package imports these types, understanding them is a prerequisite for reading any route or component.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript barrel files (`export * from '...'`) let consumers import everything from a single path (`@ronl/shared`) rather than deep module paths. This is the standard monorepo pattern for shared libraries.

tour.title: Multi-Tenant Configuration
tour.description: Tenants are the foundational unit of the platform. The static `tenants.json` configuration file maps eight organisations (Utrecht, Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Den Haag, Flevoland, and others) to their Keycloak realm URLs, Operaton engine endpoints, and feature flags. The tenant middleware in the backend reads the JWT's tenant claim and cross-checks it against this registry on every request, ensuring strict municipality-level isolation.

tour.title: JWT Authentication & JWKS Validation
tour.description: Every protected API call passes through the JWT middleware, which fetches and caches the Keycloak JWKS public keys, verifies the token signature and expiry, and attaches the decoded claims to the request context. This middleware is the security foundation of the entire API — without it, no business logic is reachable. It is the most widely imported backend module alongside the logger.
tour.languageLesson: JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) allows the API to verify JWT signatures without storing a shared secret. The public keys are fetched from Keycloak's well-known endpoint, cached in Redis, and rotated automatically when Keycloak rolls its signing keys.

tour.title: Compliance Audit Logging
tour.description: The audit middleware intercepts every HTTP response, captures the tenant ID, user ID, action, HTTP status, and IP address, and writes a structured record via the audit service to the PostgreSQL `audit_logs` table. This two-part design (middleware captures, service persists) satisfies BIO, NEN 7510, and AVG/GDPR compliance requirements. The database schema reveals exactly what fields are retained and for how long.

tour.title: Operaton BPMN Engine Service
tour.description: The Operaton service is the core integration layer between the Express API and the BPMN engine. It provides a fully-typed client covering process lifecycle (start, query, history, variables), user task management (list, claim, complete, form), DMN decision evaluation, and capacity management. Every process and task route delegates to this service, making it the busiest backend module after the logger.

tour.title: External Task Worker
tour.description: The external task worker runs as a long-polling loop alongside the HTTP server. It subscribes to Operaton service tasks by topic, picks them up when BPMN processes reach a service task step, executes the work (such as workspace provisioning), and reports completion or failure back to the engine. This is how the platform automates steps in government workflows without human intervention.
tour.languageLesson: Operaton's external task pattern is an alternative to async callbacks: the worker polls with a long-HTTP request, the engine holds the connection open until a task is available, then responds. This avoids the need for the API to be publicly reachable by the engine.

tour.title: BPMN & DMN Process Examples
tour.description: The Flevoland example processes show the platform running real government workflows end-to-end. The tree-felling permit BPMN orchestrates citizen application, caseworker review, and DMN-based eligibility decisions. The RIP Phase 1 process handles multi-phase project definitions. These files are deployed to the Operaton engine and are the business logic the API serves — reading them alongside the route handlers shows how HTTP requests map to running process instances.
tour.languageLesson: BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation) defines the flow of tasks, gateways, and events. DMN (Decision Model and Notation) separates decision logic into standalone tables that BPMN processes invoke via a `BusinessRuleTask`. Keeping decisions in DMN makes them auditable and changeable without redeploying the process.

tour.title: Frontend Auth & API Client
tour.description: On the frontend, the Keycloak service manages the OIDC Authorization Code Flow: it initialises the Keycloak.js client, handles silent token refresh, and exposes the current token. The central API client wraps axios with an interceptor that attaches the Bearer token to every request. Together these two modules are the foundation of all 28 frontend components that call the backend — every hook and page depends on them.
tour.languageLesson: The OIDC Authorization Code Flow redirects the browser to Keycloak, which authenticates the user and returns an authorization code. The frontend exchanges this code for access and refresh tokens. Keycloak.js handles token refresh automatically using a hidden iframe or silent redirect.

tour.title: React App Shell & Role-Based Routing
tour.description: The root App component defines the React Router tree and enforces role-based routing: residents are directed to the citizen Dashboard, caseworkers to CaseworkerDashboard or its V2 variant, and admins to the admin panel. It also resolves the active tenant from the URL or stored preference. This file is the top-level orchestrator of all user-facing experiences.

tour.title: AI Chat via MCP Providers
tour.description: The MCP (Model Context Protocol) layer adds AI chat capabilities powered by multiple knowledge sources. The McpProvider interface is implemented by four providers — TriplyDB SPARQL, Operaton BPMN data, LDE linked-data events, and CPRMV legislation — each spawning or connecting to a separate MCP server process. The McpRegistry manages their lifecycle, and the MCP route streams responses back to the frontend. The LlmProvider/LlmRegistry pair adds a parallel abstraction for direct LLM APIs such as Anthropic Claude.
tour.languageLesson: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard that lets AI models call external tools via a JSON-RPC interface. Each MCP server exposes a set of `tools` the LLM can invoke. The registry pattern here means the API can route a chat message to whichever provider owns the relevant tool without hard-coding provider logic in the route handler.

tour.title: Keycloak Realm & IAM Configuration
tour.description: The Keycloak realm export defines the entire identity model for the platform: the `ronl` realm, frontend and backend OIDC clients, role mappings (citizen, caseworker, admin), identity provider federation, and the custom RONL login theme. This configuration is the authoritative IAM source of truth — changes here affect which tokens are issued, which roles exist, and what the login screen looks like across all municipalities.

tour.title: Local Development Environment
tour.description: The root Docker Compose file spins up the three local infrastructure services the backend needs: Keycloak (IAM), PostgreSQL (audit logs), and Redis (JWKS cache / sessions). The backend SETUP.md walks through prerequisite installation, environment variable configuration, and the exact command sequence to get a fully running local instance. These two files are what a new developer reads on day one before writing a single line of code.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipelines & Azure Deployment
tour.description: Four GitHub Actions workflows automate the full delivery pipeline: separate build-and-deploy workflows for the backend (Azure App Service) and frontend (Azure Static Web Apps), each with acceptance and production variants. The backend pipeline compiles TypeScript, bundles the shared package, and uploads a deployment artifact; the frontend pipeline runs Vite with environment-specific `.env` files and deploys the static output. These pipelines are the final step in the journey from code commit to live government service.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions uses environment-specific workflows to enforce promotion gates: code is first deployed to the acceptance (acc) environment for testing, then to production via a separate workflow trigger. Splitting workflows by environment prevents accidental production deployments and allows environment-specific secrets.
